summary: Backend-only regression for /api/units/import robust header detection (Central Vista Farms bug). Wrote pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_units_import.py covering: (1) varied-header .xlsx with title row + 'Plot No.'/'Area (Sq. Ft)'/'Basic Price'/'Total Amount' style headers and comma-formatted numbers (30,00,000 -> 3000000), (2) .csv upload with commas, (3) classic .xlsx header regression ('UNIT NO.', 'Basic Sale Price', 'Grand Total'), (4) negative case with only 'Name,Value' returning 400 mentioning header. All 5 tests PASSED (5/5). Numeric parsing verified via GET /api/units (area_sqft=1200, bsp=3000000, infra_dev=120000 for TCVF-101; bsp=2500000 for TCVF-CSV1). Cleanup performed via Mongo (no unit DELETE endpoint exists) — CVF is back to 0 units. Existing data (Vacation Village) untouched.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1126 lines — consider splitting importer helpers (_num, COL_SYNS, _read_tabular, _detect_header) into a units_import module for maintainability.
No DELETE /api/units/{unit_id} endpoint exists; import upsert logic is fine, but ops/testing would benefit from an admin-only delete for cleanup.
_detect_header requires unit_no + >=1 more matched field which is good; consider ignoring merged/title rows explicitly (currently handled by scoring, works).
seed_data_creation: Created 4 units (TCVF-101, TCVF-102, TCVF-CSV1, TCLASSIC-1) under proj_01d7e89ba838 during tests; cleaned up via Mongo at end of run. Verified CVF now has 0 units.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for 'Header row not found in Excel' on unit import is confirmed working. Reusable pytest suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_units_import.py; the test_zzz_cleanup case wipes its own units directly in Mongo since no DELETE unit API exists.
rca of the issue: Original importer only scanned first 10 rows and required literal phrase 'basic sale price' in header, and did not accept CSV. Fix: _read_tabular now handles .xlsx and .csv, _detect_header scores first 30 rows using COL_SYNS synonyms (unit/plot + area/price/charges), _num strips commas/₹/spaces so Indian-format numbers like 30,00,000 parse to 3000000. Verified end-to-end against 4 test scenarios.
